paper.title: SONIC: Supersizing Motion Tracking for Natural Humanoid Whole-Body Control
paper.source_version: arXiv v4, revised 2026-08-13; Science Robotics 11(117), eaed4592, published 2026-08-12

decision_relevance.why_admitted: SONIC defines a concrete, high-capacity humanoid tracking trainer with explicit reference-command formats, reward terms, training parameters, deployment timing, and independent evaluation metrics. It therefore supplies a candidate frozen-trainer contract and baseline settings for both harness knobs.
not_evidence_for: An agent that searches or composes reference datasets
Automatic reward search or prompt-to-reward synthesis
Natural-language human steering of the training loop
Dynamic feasibility of arbitrary composed references
Apple-Silicon training of the reported system

mechanisms.name: Three-format motion command contract
mechanisms.description: Robot joint trajectories, SMPL human joint positions, or hybrid current upper-body keypoints plus lower-body robot trajectories are expressed in the robot-local frame and sampled over encoder-specific future horizons.

mechanisms.name: Specialized aligned encoders
mechanisms.description: Robot, human, and hybrid MLP encoders map synchronized command formats into one latent space; pairwise token and cycle-consistency losses align the modalities.

mechanisms.name: Universal FSQ token
mechanisms.description: Finite Scalar Quantization produces two 32-dimensional tokens with 32 scalar levels per dimension in the default configuration, yielding a 64-dimensional controller interface.

mechanisms.name: Proprioception-conditioned action decoder
mechanisms.description: A shared MLP combines the universal token with ten steps of proprioceptive history and outputs 29 desired joint positions for joint-level PD control.

mechanisms.name: Joint PPO and representation objective
mechanisms.description: PPO, robot-reference reconstruction, cross-encoder token alignment, and human-to-robot cycle consistency are optimized jointly with an asymmetric privileged critic.

mechanisms.name: Generic engineered tracking reward
mechanisms.description: Seven pose/velocity tracking terms and five stability or regularization penalties provide one shared reward across downstream applications.

mechanisms.name: Failure-weighted motion-bin sampling
mechanisms.description: Fixed-duration bins are sampled using capped failure weights blended with uniform coverage, concentrating practice without abandoning dataset breadth.

mechanisms.name: Short-horizon generative kinematic planner
mechanisms.description: A masked latent in-betweening model maps user commands and endpoint keyframes into 0.8-to-2.4-second motion segments that the frozen tracker consumes as references.

mechanisms.name: Unified deployment motion interface
mechanisms.description: The official deployment stack stores joint positions, velocities, root poses, and optional SMPL data in one frame-indexed MotionSequence whose encoder-mode field selects the compatible encoder.

failure_modes.name: Balance loss under extreme commands or dynamics
failure_modes.description: The tracker may lose balance under more extreme conditions or very dynamic motions despite command randomization and spring filtering.

failure_modes.name: No formal safety or energy treatment
failure_modes.description: The paper does not formally address safety or energy efficiency for extended deployment.

failure_modes.name: Non-data-matched tracker comparison
failure_modes.description: Tracker baselines use different source datasets and retargeting pipelines, confounding algorithm, data, and scaling effects.

failure_modes.name: Pose metrics exclude failed rollouts
failure_modes.description: MPJPE-L, velocity distance, and acceleration distance are reported only for successfully tracked motions because early termination makes them undefined.

failure_modes.name: High reproduction cost and partial public corpus
failure_modes.description: The largest run used approximately 21k GPU-hours, while the public 288-hour BONES-SEED subset does not equal the 611-hour training corpus.

failure_modes.name: Checkpoint and interface drift
failure_modes.description: The current release contains default, low-latency, and v1.1 variants with distinct lookahead and normalization contracts; mixing encoder, decoder, or observation config invalidates the controller contract.

evaluation.name: Largest-vs-smallest OOD scaling result
evaluation.description: On test-content, the 42M model reports 99.6% success and 23.8 mm MPJPE-L versus 98.0% and 27.7 mm for the 1.2M model.

evaluation.name: Cross-dataset tracker comparison
evaluation.description: SONIC reports 98.5%, 99.2%, and 97.2% success on test-content, test-repetition, and PHUMA; the comparison is not data-matched.

evaluation.name: Real-world motion tracking
evaluation.description: The policy completed 123 of 124 real-world motion sequences, reporting 99.2% success and 25.7 mm MPJPE-L versus 100% and 22.3 mm in simulation.

evaluation.name: Universal token versus explicit SMPL for VLA
evaluation.description: Across the three-task action-space ablation, FSQ tokens averaged 68% success versus 27% for explicit SMPL poses, a 42 percentage-point reported difference after rounding.

evaluation.name: Command-encoder comparison
evaluation.description: Robot, human, and hybrid encoders each exceed 99.2% test-content success; the hybrid encoder has 26.5 mm MPJPE-L versus 23.8 mm for robot input.

evidence.locator: Section 3.2, Motion Tracking Formulation and Universal Control Policy
evidence.claim: SONIC defines local-frame proprioceptive and motion-command states, 29 joint-position actions, PD control, a tracking reward, and three command formats.
Specialized encoders, FSQ, shared control decoder, auxiliary reference decoder, and four joint losses form the universal policy; FSQ-32-32 is the default.
The supplement reports encoder/decoder dimensions, ten-frame horizons, frame intervals, PPO settings, and adaptive-sampling parameters.
The baseline reward contains seven weighted tracking terms and five weighted penalties with explicit equations, scales, and thresholds.
The filtered training split contains 317,189 clips, 611 hours, and 100M+ frames; BONES-SEED releases a 288-hour subset.
Scaling, cross-dataset, sim-to-sim, and sim-to-real results are reported with success and motion-error metrics; baseline data are not matched.
The generative planner produces variable-length kinematic in-betweening references from context, target keyframes, and user commands.
A VLA action-space ablation reports higher task success for universal FSQ tokens than explicit SMPL poses.
The paper reports missing formal safety and energy treatment, possible balance loss, successful-rollout conditioning of pose metrics, and NVIDIA funding/patent interests.
The deployment system uses four rates and a source-agnostic MotionSequence with frame-indexed motion data and encoder-mode selection.

evidence.locator: Model Checkpoints and SONIC v1.1 Inference
evidence.claim: The official model release distinguishes default, low-latency, and v1.1 contracts and requires each encoder to be paired with its decoder and observation config.
The official code exposes named encoder configurations and separate robot and SMPL motion-library inputs for training.
The authors deposited an archival SONIC code and figure-data snapshot on Zenodo.
